correctness.rationale: The update filters only arrow targets and preserves K45. On the decreasing-sequence tree the source blocks of each agent are disjoint; each block X×Y (Y⊆X) is transitive and Euclidean. At transfinite stage ξ the block target set is exactly the children with ordinal label β≥ξ: a current child-target retains its parent-agent successor (itself) while its opposite-agent child block is nonempty precisely if ξ<β. Thus the fixed formula is true at a current target precisely if ξ<β, proving the block induction at successors and limits. For each ξ<α the root arrow to child ξ is deleted next, and at α all arrows vanish; hence exact first fixed α. For any model with ≤κ worlds, fresh deletions at all ξ<α inject α into at most κ original labelled arrows, so α<κ+. All required tree sizes fit κ. Atom-free one-agent K45 arrow targets are mutually bisimilar; modal-depth-zero formulas are global constants; either case gives h≤1. The actual extracted code checks finite ranks 0–8; infinite cases rely on ordinal proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: The natural question is the transfinite closure-ordinal spectrum for a fixed, maximally parsimonious believed-public-announcement formula. The result establishes a complete sharp cardinal spectrum rather than isolated examples, while eliminating parity atoms and nested-modal machinery from a known ω-frame. A matching one-agent/depth-zero obstruction demonstrates a structural resource threshold. This is a precise classification of update complexity directly motivated by the 2026 treatment of transfinite announcements, not an arbitrary parameter slice or rebranded finite check.
